title: Is “remixing” a better direction for AI games than generating from scratch?
author: Fearless_Shift7108
selftext:
I’ve been wondering if the most interesting part of AI in games might not be generating a full game from nothing.

Maybe the better use case is remixing: taking an existing small game idea, changing the rules, changing the world, changing the characters, or making a strange variation of it.

Generating from scratch can feel impressive, but remixing feels more playful to me. It gives people something to react to instead of starting from a blank page.

Curious what others think. For AI-assisted game creation, would you rather start from a prompt, a template, or an existing game you can remix?

comments.author: Murder_1337
comments.body: Yeah build a variant or a cross of two games would be ideal but ai game dev is usually something simple

replies.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
replies.body: I would argue that you can build complex games with AI, but success will depend on your dev and AI skills.

replies.author: Fearless_Shift7108
replies.body: Yeah, that’s kind of the direction I had in mind too — not “AI makes a huge finished game from nothing,” but more like quick variants, weird mashups, or small playable experiments. I feel like AI game tools might be more useful when they help people iterate on a simple idea fast instead of promising something massive.
